_comment: JSON, not YAML: linear_deps.py is standard-library only and runs in python:alpine, which has no YAML parser. Prose version: ticket-types.md. Checker: `linear_deps.py verify`.

generic._comment: Tool-agnostic project-management vocabulary. Nothing here names Linear: an attribute is a single-choice tag, a lot is whatever groups issues that ship together, a body section is a heading in the ticket text.

type.definition: What kind of work the ticket is. Single choice, exactly one per ticket.

addressee.definition: Who must answer or act. Single choice, only on tickets that wait on someone outside the team.

lot.definition: The set of tickets that ship together and are proved together (one delivery per lot and per environment).

types.definition: Something delivered fails to do what was promised, and the promise can be cited.
types.test: Can you fill « Expected » by citing a source: a spec, an API contract, a doc, or the behaviour before?
required_sections: In plain words, with an example

types.definition: Someone outside the team must do something: grant an access, deliver a piece of work, intervene.
types.test: Can you name who must act, what, and who waits?
required_sections: In plain words, with an example

types.definition: Someone must tell us something: a decision or an information.
types.test: Can you write it in one sentence and name who decides?
required_sections: In plain words, with an example

types.definition: We do not know yet what to do, it is ours to find out, within a time-box; the deliverable is a written decision or a proof of concept, never shipped code.
types.test: Is the deliverable a written decision or a proof of concept?
required_sections: In plain words, with an example

types.definition: A user or a client gets a capability they did not have.
types.test: Can you write « As a role, I can action »?
required_sections: In plain words, with an example

types.definition: A user or a client sees something they already have change for the better.
types.test: Could the user already do it before?
required_sections: In plain words, with an example

types.definition: Show that one thing works on one environment, by running something and looking at the result, with no code to write.
types.test: Is the work to run something and look at the result?
required_sections: In plain words, with an example

types.definition: Work that ends in a merge and brings no visible change: a slice of a feature, an upgrade, debt, tooling, infra, a data migration.
types.test: Does it end in a merge, with nothing a user notices?
required_sections: In plain words, with an example

roles.change: A ticket that ends in a merge: Bug, Feature, Improvement, Technical task. Also called a code ticket or a dev issue.
roles.waiting: A ticket that waits on someone outside the team: Question, Blocker.
roles.evidence: A ticket whose work is to observe and report: Proof.

blocks.meaning: A blocks B: B cannot be closed before A is. It says what stops the work; the ticket type never does.

related.meaning: A and B concern the same thing; no ordering.

parent.meaning: A is a sub-issue of B (a Technical task split out of a Feature).

rules.text: Every issue carries exactly one Type.
The Addressee is a single choice.

rules.subject: @waiting
rules.text: A Question or a Blocker names who must answer or act.
Addressee is used on Question and Blocker only.

rules.subject: @waiting
rules.text: A Question or a Blocker is created in the team that must answer or act.

rules.subject: Proof
rules.text: A Proof is blocked by at least one dev issue.

rules.subject: Proof
rules.text: Each Proof is blocked by every dev issue of its lot.

rules.subject: Proof
rules.text: A Proof that is Done cannot be blocked by a dev issue that is not Done.

rules.subject: @change
rules.text: Every code ticket links a recommended Proof, or says « none » and why.
A ticket body has the sections its type requires, « In plain words » first.

binding._comment: Linear specifics: label groups, template names, state names. Replace this block to bind the generic model to another tracker.

states._comment: Kinds are Linear's state types, as exported in node.state.
